description: Official facts about a US address or point: flood zone, natural-hazard ratings, weather alerts, air quality, crime rate, drinking water, internet providers, electricity price, home price trends, EV chargers, county health, childcare prices and nearby housing counselors. Use when someone is buying, renting or moving, or asks about flood or disaster risk. Send a street address, or latitude and longitude. Outside the US (a point): earthquakes, disaster alerts within 500 km and the 10-day weather risk. Also, each on request: park (a US national park's alerts, closures, fees, campgrounds); sky: true with a point (aurora chance, moon, darkness, tides); schools: true (public schools nearby; not school assignment or test scores); college (net price after aid, graduation rate, debt, earnings; add major). Send only the parts needed. Never call a place, school or college safe, good or bad; give the numbers. Not an insurance quote.

address.description: US street address with city and state, e.g. '1600 Pennsylvania Ave NW, Washington, DC 20500'

college.description: A US college's name, e.g. 'University of Washington', 'Rice University'

lat.description: Latitude, when there's no street address (e.g. the center of a ZIP or city)

major.description: A field of study at the college, for what its graduates earn and borrow, e.g. 'nursing'

park.description: A US national park or site's name or 4-letter NPS code, e.g. 'Yosemite', 'mora'

place.description: Name of the place, for the answer

schools.description: true for public schools near the address or point, closest first

sky.description: true for the night sky at the point: aurora chance, moon, darkness and, on US coasts, tides

state.description: Two-letter state to narrow a common college name, e.g. 'WA'

name: check_place
title: Place check: hazards, weather, schools, parks and the night sky
